source.title: Feature Learning in Infinite-Width Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent garbling or cutoff.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analytically derives infinite-width training behavior and reports finite-width comparisons, but it studies feature learning and parametrization stability rather than training classification error on CIFAR benchmarks.
record.gate_note: Reports CIFAR-10 square-loss accuracy while sweeping learning rate and width to verify maximum stable learning-rate scaling (row R1). The Omniglot and Word2Vec experiments compare feature-learning and kernel limits on transfer tasks, not training classification error as Versions 1–6 define it. Theory statements and cited studies are not additional experimental rows.
record.test_reason: The study's own results concern parametrization, feature learning and learning-rate scaling with width. R1 measures validation accuracy and maximum learning-rate scaling, without comparing rates to the initial linearized stability threshold or measuring recovery, curvature or edge-of-stability dynamics. Neither these results nor the transfer experiments test V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. Qualify the theoretical conclusion: stable standard and NTK parametrizations yield kernel limits without feature learning for training times independent of width. µP admits feature learning, and its infinite-width limit outperforms the tested kernel baselines on Word2Vec and Omniglot, with finite-width performance approaching the limit.
record.recipe_differences: Uses parametrization scaling and infinite-width limit analysis, with CIFAR10 square-loss accuracy as a learning-rate stability check; it does not use the benchmark classification-error recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Width and parametrization change the reported maximum learning-rate scaling in the CIFAR10 accuracy sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: For two-hidden-layer ReLU MLPs trained with square loss on CIFAR-10, the maximum learning rate scales inversely with width under SP and remains constant under µP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Network parametrization determines how the maximum usable learning rate scales with width.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix E argues that iid middle-layer weights scaled as 1/n produce vanishing preactivations and, with more than two hidden layers, vanishing gradients in the infinite-width limit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization scaling with width can make multilayer infinite-width training remain at initialization.

record.problems: The CIFAR10 result is presented as a figure with accuracy curves and a textual description of learning-rate scaling; exact accuracy values and uncertainty are not stated in the supplied text. It does not report training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying rows identified. Omniglot and Word2Vec report transfer-task accuracy, which does not measure the outcomes named by the listed claim versions; the paper's mathematical results and cited prior work are not separate experimental rows.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels and effects of model size or training recipe.
Spurious local minima in ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction through extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts, special initialization or Fixup.
Activation-matched initialization effects on training speed and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization and very deep convolutional networks.
Recovery above the initial linearized stability threshold, transient loss and curvature changes, edge-of-stability trajectories and divergence relative to that threshold.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's stability definition concerns bounded activations and logits as width increases at fixed training time; it explicitly permits divergence with time. This does not establish V5's temporal stability or recovery behavior. Appendix E concerns width scaling rather than the activation-matched initialization and training-speed/depth comparisons in V4.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test training classification error, corrupted or random labels, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, model size effects on fitting, or early stopping/regularized recipes.
Does not test teacher-student two-layer ReLU problems, spurious minima, or student width relative to teacher width.
Does not compare plain and residual networks for training error or test special initialization, shortcuts, or normalization on that outcome.
Does not test activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, or trainable depth as stated in this version.
Does not test learning rates relative to a stability threshold, loss curvature trajectories, or divergence near that threshold.
Does not test batch normalization's effect on accuracy speed or learning-rate tolerance, or Fixup residual networks.

rows.subject: relu MLP with 2 hidden layers
rows.operation_detail: Swept learning rate and width under the standard and maximal-update parametrizations, training with square loss on CIFAR10; reported accuracy against learning rate.

conditions.value: Standard Param and Maximal Update Param

rows.measure: accuracy as a function of learning rate; maximum learning rate scaling
rows.value: Text states that maximum learning rate for SP scales like 1/width and is constant in µP; plotted accuracy curves are figure only.
rows.locator: Section 1, Figure titled “Verifying Max Learning Rate for P and SP”
rows.note: The text describes the maximum learning-rate scaling, but gives no numeric accuracy values or training classification error. The plotted curves are not transcribed.
rows.check: Specify validation accuracy: the figure axes say 'valid acc'. The text establishes inverse-width maximum learning-rate scaling for SP and constant scaling for µP, but this measure cannot establish any listed version's effect. The qualitative scaling result is readable even though exact accuracy values are unavailable.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
